kept.excerpt: National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) presidential candidate Brian Mundubile on Saturday officially launched his campaign during a rally at Kitwe Playing Fields (KPF), drawing large crowds of supporters. Among those who attended the rally were Tonse Alliance Vice President Chifumu Banda, United Liberal Party president Sakwiba Sikota, Economic Freedom Fighters president Kasonde Mwenda, and Green Party leader Peter Sinkamba, among other alliance leaders.
kept.relevance: Documents Mundubile’s active campaign and support from multiple opposition party leaders, while rally attendance alone does not establish national voting support.

kept.excerpt: In a statement dated 27 May 2026, the Commission said the allegations which circulated on the Patriotic Front’s official Facebook page were malicious and bore no resemblance to any action taken or contemplated by the institution. The ECZ noted that its Chairperson, Mrs. Mwangala Zaloumis SC, acting in her capacity as Returning Officer for the presidential election, had herself formally declared Mr. Mundubile and Mr. Zulu as duly nominated candidate and running mate during the recently concluded nomination exercise.
kept.publisher: Lusaka Times, reproducing an Electoral Commission of Zambia statement
kept.relevance: Clarifies Mundubile’s legal candidacy status and records the electoral commission’s rejection of claims that it planned to disqualify his ticket.

kept.excerpt: THE Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has validated the nomination of Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu as presidential candidate and running mate, respectively, under the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP). Earlier, ECZ also validated the nomination of Harry Kalaba and his running mate Moses Mawere under the Citizens First (CF) ticket.
kept.relevance: Independently confirms Mundubile’s approved presidential nomination, running mate and ballot party, alongside another opposition ticket.

kept.excerpt: IF elections were held today, President Hakainde Hichilema would win with 60 percent of the vote, compared to 35 percent for opposition candidates. This is according to a new national poll conducted by independent consultants under the supervision of leading demographer Dr Namuunda Mutombo of the University of Zambia. The poll was conducted between 2nd and 15th October 2025, interviewing 1,009 adults aged 18 and above across all 10 provinces and 49 districts. Face-to-face household interviews were carried out with a margin of error of ±3.1 percent.
kept.relevance: Provides a methodologically described incumbent-support baseline, although its October 2025 fieldwork predates Mundubile’s selection and cannot establish his support near the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: In Zambia’s August 2021 general elections, longtime opposition leader Hakainde Hichilema won the presidential race with 59% of votes—after five prior unsuccessful runs. In concurrent National Assembly elections, his United Party for National Development (UPND) party won a majority; it holds 56% of 165 seats, including appointed ones.
kept.publisher: U.S. Congressional Research Service, archived by EveryCRSReport
kept.relevance: Establishes the incumbent’s previous electoral strength and a historical example of an opposition candidate defeating Zambia’s governing party.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-08-04, inclusive. Publication dates were checked using displayed article dates, source document dates or page metadata; dates above are publication dates, and the poll’s earlier fieldwork dates are stated separately. Web search was used for discovery and dated source text. web_fetch failed because of a provider-configuration error; the agent-reach web-read fallback verified the News Diggers nomination report and Zambia Monitor campaign-launch report before its retrieval backends became temporarily unavailable. Other included excerpts were verified in dated search-index text. The News Diggers excerpt is from the publicly accessible introduction; the remainder is paywalled. Later-dated expert previews, later-updated election guides, undated pages, post-cutoff reporting and dynamic related-story content were excluded. No prediction-market pages, betting odds or market prices are included. No recent nationally representative poll specifically measuring Mundubile’s support was verified by the cutoff; candidate statements and rally crowds were not treated as representative polls.
